$comment: Machine-readable definition of Sightline Prompter script directives. Human spec: SCRIPT-DIRECTIVES.md. AI brief: AI-SCRIPT-BRIEF.md.
name: sightline-script-directives
status: syntax agreed; implemented in the app (27 October 2026): pause, marker, wpm, target, pacing, mode

sections.markdown: A level-2 heading (## ) starts a section
sections.plainTextAndWord: A line starting '=== SECTION' starts a section
sections.directivePlacement: At the end of the heading line, or alone on the next line

scopes.script: Before the first section: one directive line, or YAML front matter in markdown
scopes.section: On or straight after a section heading

record.description: Optional explicit OBS recording action. Requires OBS mode and recording controls. Executes only while reading reaches it, never on load. Off and pause hold prompting; use Play to continue. Unsupported pause requests leave prompting held with an error.

pacing.description: section: per-section timers and targets for batch or modular recording. session: whole-script timing for one continuous take.

wpm.description: Target words per minute. Inline, it applies until the end of the current section.

target.description: Target duration (m:ss). Script scope is used in session mode. If a section has both target and wpm, target wins.

pause.description: With no value: the same as {stop}. With a value: stop for that many seconds, with a countdown, then carry on (say "Prompter, go" to carry on sooner, or "Prompter, pause" to wait). In section mode the section timer stops too. In voice scrolling a timed pause doesn't hold, because the text only moves when the speaker does: it shows as a beat mark and the speaker takes the beat. With no value it holds in both modes.

page.description: Notes mode: start a new page here, without a heading. (A # heading also starts a page.)

stop.description: Stop here until the speaker carries on: say "Prompter, go" (or just "go"), or press Space, the clicker or the remote. Works in steady and voice scrolling. The same as {pause} with no value.

marker.description: A bookmark for retakes; Ctrl+B cycles through them. An optional label, {marker: Setup}, names it in the take log and the edit pack's marks.

listen.description: off: before an ad-lib, a demo or questions. The microphone is muted (nothing is listened to) and the prompter holds, in steady and voice scrolling; Space, a clicker, the remote or the Stream Deck carries on from the next {listen: on}, where voice following picks up again. The take log and edit pack record the time off script. on: where reading from the script starts again.

soundcheck.description: A stop that checks the microphone first, in steady and voice scrolling. room: the room's background noise, measured for 5 seconds while the speaker stays quiet; quiet (below -55 dB), ok, or noisy (above -45 dB). voice: the speaker reads a line on the card at their normal level for 7 seconds; good, too quiet, loud or clipping, with advice about voice and background noise. Continue anyway accepts a warning without forcing gain; the log retains acceptance and measurements. The result shows on a card; "Prompter, again" or Check again measures again, and Space or "Prompter, go" carries on. Each result goes in the take log (soundChecks) and the edit pack. Put {soundcheck: room} then {soundcheck: voice} at the top of a recording script, on their own lines.

prompter.description: Run a prompter command as the reading reaches this point: slower or faster (the steady speed), bigger or smaller (the text), or marker. In voice scrolling it runs when the word before it is said.

mode.description: script: read word for word with scrolling. notes (points is the same): show a page at a time with no scrolling, for speaking from notes. A page starts at a # heading or {page}; each ## heading on it is a bullet. With neither, each ## section is its own page. The page timer and {target} still apply.

rules: Curly braces are reserved for directives.
Square brackets never control the app; [Pause.] is only a note to the speaker.
HTML production comments show paused, hide during delivery and never supply spoken words or executable directives.
Unknown directives are hidden and flagged with a warning in the editor.
Use either target or wpm on a section, not both.
